focused_checks.reason: Primary read Definition 2.1, Theorem 1.3, (7.1), and the complete interpolation/contradiction passages on pp.22-24. At s=3, the weights 3/2 and -1/2 at nodes 3,9 give a positive exponential remainder, while the printed first-derivative formula is strictly negative for every allowed intermediate point. The specified 0,3,9,33 nodes satisfy the stated value and spacing inequalities. This is a decisive failure of a proof identity, not an AF geometric counterexample. The proposed bounded interpolation functional annihilates all degree <=s-2 polynomials; subtracting a Taylor polynomial and using the actual weighted Holder seminorm gives rho^{-q-(s-2)-beta}. Since the source chooses beta<alpha with q>n-1-s-beta, this contradicts its upstream rho^{3-n} lower bound. The repair is sound for this step conditional on (7.1) and the radial asymptotics; no whole geometric proof certification is claimed. The initial script and actual output were read, not rerun.

Primary checked the unrestricted 'any initial data set' quantifier in Theorem 3.3 and the general graph metric in Theorem 3.4. Schur complementation gives |grad u|^2=(F+2 ell_u-|grad_y ell|^2)^{-1}, and Ric_uu=-Delta_y F/2 yields the stated normal contraction. With F=1+(1+|y|^2)^(-1/2), ell=u/2, the induced complete positive graph metric and nonnegative null-dust stress satisfy those local/general-slice hypotheses; at the origin actual mu=1/2 differs from 3/4. AF is not required there and is not falsely claimed. Lemma 6.6 and p.26 already use the correct factor, limiting the impact.

Primary read the metric block in (6.8) and independently multiplied the f=2,Y=(1,0) SPD example: the printed candidate gives entries 3/4 off-diagonal and 7/4 in the lower block. The Schur-complement inverse has I+f^{-2}YY^T. Its first row agrees with the printed row used for the gradient identity, so the report correctly avoids claiming a downstream embedding failure.
